name: Rice
description: The primary staple cereal crop of India, grown extensively in wetlands and irrigated alluvial plains.

optimalConditions.soil: Clayey loam, alluvial soil with high water retention capacity

source: ICAR - Indian Institute of Rice Research (IIRR)

name: Cotton
description: Major commercial cash crop known as 'White Gold', cultivated in black cotton soils across western and central India.

optimalConditions.soil: Deep black soils (Regur), well-drained fertile loam

source: ICAR - Central Institute for Cotton Research (CICR)

name: Soybean
description: Important protein and edible oil crop prominent in central India (Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra).

optimalConditions.soil: Well-drained fertile loamy soil with neutral pH (6.5 - 7.5)

source: ICAR - Indian Institute of Soybean Research (IISR)

name: Maize
description: Known as the 'Queen of Cereals' due to high genetic yield potential, utilized for food, poultry feed, and industrial starch.

optimalConditions.soil: Deep, rich, well-drained fertile sandy loam to clay loam

source: ICAR - Indian Institute of Maize Research (IIMR)

name: Tomato
description: High-value commercial vegetable crop grown across diverse climatic zones in India.

optimalConditions.soil: Well-drained sandy loam rich in organic matter (pH 6.0 - 7.0)

source: ICAR - Indian Institute of Horticultural Research (IIHR)

name: Chilli
description: Universal culinary spice and cash crop widely cultivated in southern and western India.

optimalConditions.soil: Well-aerated, well-drained loam or light clay soil with rich organic content
